body.estimand_functional: For \( (G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}} \), let \( (\widehat G,\mathcal T)=\operatorname{RankPeel}(P_X,R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}) \).  The identifying equality \(\theta_G=[\widehat G]\) holds on either of two strict subclasses: first, the abstract query-local subclass satisfying first-jet determinacy and latent-separator-relative pointwise fibre coherence; second, the positive-density/open-support subclass in which every queried predictor law is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on an open full-measure set.  On the second subclass, directed Markovness and the conditional-sufficiency factorization yield the separator rank bound without pointwise fibre coherence.  Outside the union of these subclasses, RankPeel is only a partial oracle-relative procedure and no identifying equality is asserted.

sampling_model.design: Population observational identification; there is no intervention or randomization design.
sampling_model.units: One scalar random vector indexed by the finite layered vertex set, with only \(X\) observed.
sampling_model.treatment: None; the target is the causal structure rather than a treatment effect.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None in the population theorem.  The partial functional \(R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}\) is determined by the observed law only on \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), and oracle evaluation cost is excluded from query complexity.  Structural recovery holds either under query-local first-jet determinacy plus latent-separator-relative pointwise fibre coherence, or under the strict positive-density/open-support condition for every queried predictor law; the second route derives version stability and the separator upper bound from directed Markovness and conditional sufficiency.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The full binary adjacency matrix is identifiable up to permutation of latent variables, using measured pure descendants as recursive surrogates in an exhaustive subset construction.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: RankPeel gives the same structural target with a quadratic oracle schedule on two explicit strict subclasses: the abstract query-local first-jet-determining and fibre-coherent subclass, and the positive-density/open-support subclass where the almost-sure sufficient-statistic factorization suffices without pointwise fibre coherence.  The anchor's full-class promise is not claimed for the present all-version law functional.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The proposed algorithm can find the correct Markov equivalence class of the whole graph asymptotically under proper restrictions.
The estimated variable and the true variable are equivalent up to an invertible transformation.

body.tldr: Prashant, Ng, Zhang, and Huang already identify the full binary adjacency matrix of a nonlinear latent hierarchy and already reuse measured pure descendants as higher-layer surrogates.  RankPeel is a deterministic population protocol with at most \(p^2+p\) combined observed-law queries, worst-case \(\Theta(p^2)\) query order, and \(O(p^3)\) bookkeeping.  This note corrects and qualifies a version-free reading of the anchor's Conditions 1--3: the smooth boundary member \(X_1=\cdots=X_4=H\) admits conditional-mean versions with different transverse Jacobian ranks, so the unchanged conditions do not by themselves define the present law-level rank oracle.  Exact recovery has two proved strict-subclass routes.  The sharp abstract route assumes query-local first-jet determinacy and latent-separator-relative pointwise fibre coherence.  The new support-regular route assumes that every queried predictor law is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on an open full-measure set; positive density then fixes first jets, and directed Markovness plus the anchor's almost-sure conditional-sufficiency factorization yields the separator bound without pointwise fibre coherence.  Canonical neutrality, quadratic complexity, and oracle-relative replay retain their stated scope.

project_justification.gap: The closest nonlinear result already identifies the complete binary adjacency matrix and already uses measured pure descendants recursively, but its construction exhaustively searches subset families and gives no explicit polynomial observed-query budget.  In addition, the anchor's Conditions 1--3 do not make the present all-version conditional-mean Jacobian rank a functional of the observed law on lower-dimensional predictor supports: smooth versions can agree almost surely while having different transverse derivatives.
project_justification.niche: A deterministic pairwise and canonical-deletion protocol gives a quadratic population-query schedule.  Its exact law-level recovery is separated into a sharp abstract query-regular theorem and a transparent positive-density/open-support theorem; the latter derives rather than assumes the needed first-jet uniqueness and uses the anchor's almost-sure sufficient-statistic factorization rather than pointwise fibre coherence.
project_justification.fill: The contribution proves an almost-everywhere bottleneck theorem, derives first-jet determinacy from positive queried densities, and proves the restricted separator upper bound from directed Markovness and conditional sufficiency on that support-regular subclass.  Combined with the private-path lower bounds, this yields exact canonical RankPeel recovery with at most \(p^2+p\) calls, worst-case \(\Theta(p^2)\) query order, and \(O(p^3)\) bookkeeping.  The abstract first-jet-determining and fibre-coherent theorem and the legal full-class boundary counterexample are retained, so no unchanged-class strict-tightening claim is made.

body.related_work: Prashant, Ng, Zhang, and Huang identify the full binary adjacency matrix up to latent permutation and use measured pure descendants as higher-layer surrogates.  RankPeel changes the construction to deterministic pair tests and canonical parent deletion and proves a quadratic oracle budget.  The present \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\) is a formalized comparison class keyed to their structural and analytic conditions; it is not an assertion that the paper defined the present all-version observed-law rank functional.  The boundary witness corrects a version-free transfer of their separator argument, while the positive-density theorem shows that their almost-sure conditional-sufficiency factorization does supply the required rank upper bound on an open full-dimensional queried support, without pointwise fibre coherence.  Huang, Low, Xie, Glymour, and Zhang inform the pure-descendant surrogate motif in a linear \(\mathrm{IL}^{2}\mathrm H\) model, but their covariance-rank assumptions and Markov-equivalence target differ.  Kong, Huang, Xie, Xing, Chi, and Zhang identify nonlinear latent representations only up to invertible transformations rather than through this observed conditional-mean rank protocol.  Sullivant, Talaska, and Draisma motivate the separation between graph-forced rank upper bounds and generic path-based lower bounds in the linear Gaussian case.  Hatcher's invariance-of-domain theorem and Rudin's inverse-function theorem support the topological arguments; neither source supplies the causal query-regularity or support assumptions.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The prescribed early-kill audit covered all \(676\) stated three-level graphs and all \(60{,}892\) enumerated level-zero and retained-surrogate cuts without a \(d\)-separation counterexample, but finite enumeration is not the recursive graphical proof.  Analytically, the unchanged Conditions 1--3 do not determine the present law-level Jacobian rank across conditional-mean versions: the explicit smooth boundary model \(X_1=\cdots=X_4=H\) yields valid pair representatives of ranks one and two.  The positive-density/open-support theorem excludes that defect and derives an almost-everywhere separator bound; the more abstract theorem still requires query-local first-jet determinacy and latent-separator-relative pointwise fibre coherence.  No blanket separator-equals-rank identity, extra saturated-rank condition, faithfulness inheritance after contraction, finite-sample Jacobian rate, oracle evaluation algorithm, or image-data consistency is asserted.
body.honest_scope: The causal target is the full layered adjacency matrix modulo within-layer latent permutations.  The proved identifying map is RankPeel on the union of two explicit strict subclasses of the formalized anchor class: the query-local first-jet-determining and latent-separator-relative fibre-coherent subclass, and the positive-density/open-support subclass for which every actually queried predictor law is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on an open full-measure set.  The second route does not assume pointwise fibre coherence.  The unchanged formalized class contains the equal-measurement boundary model on which RankPeel requests a version-unstable pair and returns \(\bot\), so completeness and exact recovery are not claimed there.  The \(p^2+p\) call count, \(O(p^3)\) bookkeeping bound, and replay completeness remain unconditional properties of the partial oracle procedure; structural soundness requires one of the two strict-subclass routes.  Alternate representatives outside the law-stable domain, alternate deletion orders, counterfactual candidate states, oracle evaluation time, nonparametric estimation, finite-sample recovery, and CelebA consistency are outside scope.
body.interpretation: On either proved strict subclass, equality of the canonical baseline and augmented ranks certifies that the currently tested candidate set contains every parent of the processed mixed child, while a failed equality identifies an omitted parent.  The positive-density route is especially transparent: equality of smooth conditional-mean versions is first-order unique on the open queried support, and the almost-sure sufficient-statistic factorization has Jacobian rank at most the statistic dimension.  The transcript certifies deterministic consistency with the same population oracle; it does not certify the latent fibre-coherence condition, the positive-density support condition, or membership in the anchor class.
